text.p: Carbide/Graphite Group Inc said on Monday it plans to build a $28 million longitudinal graphitizing facility to replace less efficient Acheson graphitizing facilities.
The project, which is subject to regulatory and environmental approvals, will be funded from internal cash flow and credit facilities, the company said in a statement.

Walter Flower, the company's chief executive, said the new facility would provide "a manufacturing cost advantage of almost 20 cents a pound, a shorter inventory cycle of eight days versus 24 days, as well as significant processing advantages."
Carbide/Graphite is currently involved in two other modernization projects in its graphite electrode facilities, the company said.
Carbide/Graphite manufactures industial graphite and calcium carbide products.
